reviewer: Codex manual text cover and motion-sheet review
method: Compared eight actual 320x180 rendered covers and aligned five-frame motion sheets at 0.08, 0.30, 0.55, 0.85 and 1.15 seconds; checked titles remain legible through the common fade.

decisions.observation: Warm gold serif lettering has a dark, broad edge and drop shadow; it stays readable on the dark stage and differs from the red flame and silver styles.
Cyan glyph interiors with saturated magenta edging form a distinct electric sign treatment; unlike the single-hue violet title, both hues remain visible after fade-in.
After reducing its outline, the pink glyphs and narrow turquoise border remain separately readable; the seven-degree tilt and two-color treatment distinguish it from the straight mint title.
Orange lettering sits on a thick deep-red outline with a slight clockwise tilt; its warm red silhouette is distinct from the gold serif style.
Pale mint lettering and blue-green border make a cool, level title; the glyphs stay legible and the hue and pose differ from the tilted pink-blue candy version.
Lavender lettering with a deep violet edge and clockwise tilt reads as a purple single-palette title, separate from neon's cyan-magenta pairing.
Bright silver-white serif letters with a slate outline and strong dark shadow provide a neutral metallic treatment distinct from all saturated-color styles.
The hot-pink slab around yellow letters and counterclockwise tilt creates a high-contrast pop title; it has a different shape and palette from the blue-pink candy lettering.
